Description: FR7: 'Share order on WhatsApp' opens WhatsApp with no contact. Four of the five distributors have masked placeholder numbers (for example +91 98XXX XX318), so the link is wa.me/?text=... with no phone number. The order text is right and the order is saved as Sent, but the BRD says Share opens WhatsApp with the distributor's number. Nothing tells the owner the number is missing.
Steps to reproduce: Sign in as the demo owner > Reorder > Share order on WhatsApp for Lakshmi Dairy Distributors > look at the WhatsApp address: no phone number.
Fix (prompt #, commit): Prompt 30, commit f102836: a plain note under Share says when no real WhatsApp number is saved; 10-digit Indian numbers now get the country code 91 (WhatsApp needs it). lib/whatsapp.ts with 6 tests.
Re-test result: Live 20 Nov (build f102836): the note is now shown (before: none). WhatsApp still opens with no contact, because the demo distributors only have masked placeholder numbers, so the BRD wording 'opens WhatsApp with the distributor's number' is still NOT met on the demo data. Evidence B01_before.png, B01_after.png.
Workaround: Save a real 10-digit WhatsApp number for each distributor (More > Distributors). The app now builds the link with 91 in front. Do not invent numbers for the demo: a made-up number can reach a stranger.

Description: Every tap on 'Share order on WhatsApp' saves a NEW order, even when the button says 'Sent as ... share again'. Sharing the same list twice makes two orders for the same items, so 'on order' is doubled and tomorrow's reorder quantities are too low.
Steps to reproduce: Reorder > Share order on WhatsApp for one distributor > tap the same button again > Deliveries shows two open orders for the same items.
Fix (prompt #, commit): Prompt 31, commit b65b079: the first tap saves one order; later taps only open WhatsApp again with the saved text; quantity boxes are locked once the order is saved. lib/share-order.ts with 3 tests.
Re-test result: Live 20 Nov (build b65b079): first tap order e5bbc2ea..., second tap the SAME order; Deliveries 0 before, 1 after (1 new order). Before the fix: 2 new orders. Pass. Evidence B02_before.png, B02_after.png.

Description: Sales saved on the phone while offline can be sent twice. If the page is reloaded at the moment the network returns, the page load and the 'online' event both send the queue: 3 offline taps recorded 4 sales (stock fell by 4).
Steps to reproduce: Sell as helper > go offline > tap one item 3 times (3 waiting) > come back online and reload the page at once > stock falls by 4, not 3. With the page left open it works (2 taps = 2 sales).
Fix (prompt #, commit): Prompt 32, commits 5e15a18 then e00c48f: each offline sale carries the moment it was tapped; the server treats the same person + item + moment as the same sale, so a second send changes nothing; one sender at a time (browser lock); a failed sale stays on the phone. lib/offline-queue.ts, lib/sale-time.ts, 15 tests. No database change.
Re-test result: Live 20 Nov (build e00c48f), 3 runs of '3 offline taps, network back + reload at once': run 1 recorded 1 extra sale (a leftover from my first attempt 5e15a18, which re-sent a sale after 30 s: that attempt was not enough and was replaced); runs 2 and 3: 3 saved of 3, queue empty. Before the fix: 4 saved of 3. Evidence B03_before.png, B03_after.png.

Description: Uploading the same sales CSV twice saves every row twice with no warning, and there is no way in the app to undo an upload. Stock falls twice and the sales history is doubled.
Steps to reproduce: Stock > Upload past sales > choose a file with 3 rows > upload the same file again: '3 rows saved' both times, stock falls by 6 each time.
Fix (prompt #, commit): Prompt 33, commit 4905ead: rows an earlier CSV upload already saved (same item, date, quantity) are skipped and the screen says how many. lib/csv-dedupe.ts with 8 tests; live and demo store; the speed test now allows the two raw sales reads in addSale and importSales (page loads still read sales only through shop_snapshot).
Re-test result: Live 20 Nov (build 4905ead): first upload '3 rows saved', stock 114 -> 108; same file again '0 rows saved, 3 rows were already saved by an earlier upload, so they were skipped', stock stays 108. Before the fix: 3 rows saved again, stock 108 -> 102. Pass. Evidence B04_before.png, B04_after.png.

Description: A user of another shop who calls the 'stop selling item' route with shop 1's item id gets '200 ok', although nothing is changed (the database refuses it silently). No data leaked or changed (checked in the database), but the answer should be an error, not ok.
Steps to reproduce: Signed in as a user of a second shop, send DELETE /api/items?id=<shop 1 item id>: answer is {"ok":true}; shop 1's item stays active.
Device: Local copy of main (same code) against the live database
Workaround: None needed: no data of another shop is changed (checked in the database). Ignore the 'ok' answer.

Steps to reproduce: Owner > More > Distributors > Arjun. Or read the distributors table.
Workaround: More > Distributors > Arjun: remove or mask the real number before the demo. I did not change your data.

Description: A quick double tap on a Sell tile records two sales. Each tap is a sale, there is no undo and no short pause, so an accidental double tap at a busy counter overstates sales and takes extra stock off.
Steps to reproduce: Sell > double-tap Soft Drink: stock falls by 2.
Workaround: Tap once and wait for 'Saved' before the next tap.

Description: The Forecast Desk is not meaningfully better than a simple average. Back-test on the live shop's history (last 14 days, 30 items): Desk 2.600 units missed per item per day against 2.632 for the 14-day average (1.2% lower; the BRD target is at least 10% lower) and 2.594 for the 28-day average (the Desk is 0.2% worse). The scorecard shows the same (4.39 against 4.38). The BRD fallback 'use the simple average if the Desk is worse' is not built.
Steps to reproduce: Run the back-test in docs/m4/l2-calc.xlsx (sheet back-test), or open More > Scorecard and read Forecast error.
Fix (prompt #, commit): Not fixed: needs a decision from you first (see the summary)
Workaround: Explain it honestly in the presentation: Forecast error on the Scorecard shows the real numbers (Desk 1.2% better than a 14-day average and 0.2% worse than the 28-day average on the 20 Nov back-test; the 10% target is not met). Not fixed today because: the BRD names two different 'simple averages' (14-day in the KPI table, 28-day in A4); a per-item fallback changes every forecast and order quantity on the live shop and, chosen on the same 14 days it is judged on, tends to follow noise; and lib/forecast/desk.ts may not change without your say-so.

Description: Selling an item that has 0 stock is accepted without a message: the sale is saved, stock stays 0. This keeps stock from going negative but means the shelf count and the sales have drifted apart and the helper is not told.
Steps to reproduce: Sell as helper > tap an item whose stock is 0 > 'Saved'.
Workaround: Record the delivery first, then the sale; or check the shelf count.

Workaround: More > Festival calendar > Coming up > Remove 'Deepavali 20 Nov 2026' (product team). I did not change your data.
